The cell had joined the load's number to the unit of the value; the typed load (0.45 MPa) and the value were right. Read by an AI agent (Claude, re-center lane 4), not a person. Corrected 2026-09-27 (m192-the-test-bar-settings) against the source: Specimen / print parameters holds what p. 1 prints under "Printed Specimen Conditions", the conditions its test specimens were printed under (D63), which m170 took out of the product's print profile. Flagged physically implausible 2026-10-18 (m439, D55, D149): the sheet prints a heat deflection of 80 °C at 0.45 MPa beside its own glass transition of 55 °C (DSC), on bars its "Printed Specimen Conditions" block prints on a 23 °C bed, and states no annealing. A glassy PLA bar deflects near its glass transition (this database's 98 PLA pairs: a median of 4 °C below it, none of the glassy ones more than 5 °C above); 25 °C above it is a crystallised (annealed or moulded) bar's, which the page does not say this was. Kept as printed; it backs nothing.

polymer.basis: Classification and typical values from polymer handbooks and resin data sheets, as compiled for the estimate model (docs/audits/2026-09-15-filtering-estimates-data/physics/). The document cited prints a density inside the range, not its ends. NatureWorks Ingeo 3D850 (R-NATUREWORKS-INGEO-3D850-TDS), a PLA grade for 3D-printing monofilament, prints a specific gravity of 1.24 (ASTM D792), a peak melt temperature of 165-180 °C and a glass transition temperature of 55-60 °C (both ASTM D3418), p. 1. It prints no water absorption. PLA is semicrystalline and prints amorphous (D158): the melting point column holds 165 °C, the low end of the printed range, a ceiling every grade of the range stays under. The same page says that annealing "in the range of 176-266°F (80-130°C) can be used to promote crystallization": the annealing threshold is the glass transition's low end, 55 °C, at or below which nothing crystallises (D158).
